goldens: Race condition: Multiple concurrent requests could pass the device count check simultaneously and create devices beyond the limit. Consider using a database transaction or lock.

With this PR, ErrDeviceLimitReached is a normal failure. The rejected device is cached for 29 minutes, and its next request returns nil at the cache check. Anonymous access is then granted without the device being registered, so the limit is bypassed. Transient DB errors are cached the same way. Set the cache entry only after a successful write, or delete it on error.

[pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go:109] The limit check is not atomic. CountDevices and the upsert are separate statements with no transaction or lock. Concurrent first requests from many new devices can all see count < limit and all insert, so the limit is exceeded. Do the check and insert in one transaction, or use a conditional insert such as INSERT ... SELECT ... WHERE (SELECT COUNT(*)) < limit.

[pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go:95] updateDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached whenever RowsAffected == 0. That also happens for a device whose row is older than the 30-day window, and on MySQL when an UPDATE changes no values, because MySQL reports changed rows rather than matched rows. Both cases are reported as limit reached, so a legitimate existing device is rejected with the wrong error. Distinguish 'device not found or expired' from other zero-row outcomes.

[pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go:44] Device tagging moved from an async goroutine with its own 2-minute timeout to a synchronous call on the request context inside Authenticate. Every new or cache-expired anonymous device now blocks the request on a COUNT plus a write. A slow DB or a cancelled request context delays or fails anonymous requests. Errors that are not ErrDeviceLimitReached are only logged, so this is a latency regression. The raw ErrDeviceLimitReached is returned as-is, so it may surface as a generic 500 rather than an authn failure.
